Your transmitter relies on Bluetooth to communicate with your smartphone. This means that you need to keep your phone's Bluetooth turned on and to keep your phone nearby to stay informed.

Bluetooth connection can be disrupted by distance, thick walls, or the presence of too many other Bluetooth connected devices.

In the top left corner of your Status screen there is a bluetooth symbol. The symbol glows turquoise when your phone and transmitter are connected.

When your transmitter loses connection, it has the ability to broadcast its location to your smartphone, so that they can reconnect automatically when they come back into range.

To ensure the most reliable connection to keep you informed, it is recommended to set location access for TestProduct to 'Always' in your phones settings.

After showering, bathing or swimming, thoroughly dry the connector flap on your sensor layer before reattaching your transmitter. \n\nPlace a thin cotton cloth or absorbing paper (e.g. toilet paper or kitchen paper towel) between the white flap and the sensor layer and press down. When applied to your skin under your baseplate, the TestProduct sensor layer looks out
for signs of leakage – sending notifications to your phone via your transmitter.

As well as notifying you about leakages detected, TestProduct may sometimes give you other notifications about what is happening on your sensor layer. Understanding a little more about what these messages mean can help you decide what action to take.

TestProduct will detect change under your baseplate, but won’t always be able to tell for certain if it’s output, sweat or something else. In this case, you’ll be notified that there ‘might’ be a leak developing.\n\nTestProduct will still seek to keep you informed of any further developments – for example, notifying you if leakage is detected for certain on other parts of your baseplate. However, it is important to bear in mind that the sensors which detected the initial possible leakage are now ‘used’ and unlikely to be able to detect any further leakage. To keep fully informed in this scenario, and have the full protection of all the available sensors, you might want to change your sensor layer.

Over time, your sensor layer might get exposed to moisture from your skin and/or your stoma. If too much moisture is absorbed by the sensor layer over time, the sensors can wear out and become unable to detect output and notify you if a leakage is developing. In this case, you will be notified that your sensor layer’s sensors are ‘worn out’.\n\nYour baseplate might still be adhering to your skin but the sensors are no longer active. To keep fully informed in this scenario, you might want to change your sensor layer.

Due to coming into contact with wet skin or your stoma during application to the body, sensors are already ‘used’ and no longer able to detect leakage.

If your Status reads ‘Inner sensors are wet’, only the inner sensors have been affected and the outer sensors are still functioning.

If your Status reads ‘Your skin is wet’, all sensors have been affected – in which case you might want to change your sensor layer to stay informed.

Pay close attention to apply your baseplate and sensor layer to clean, dry skin. For helpful advice read ‘Dry applying tips’.

Due to either an issue in production, transportation, storage or handling and application, the sensor layer you’ve applied is physically broken, and unable to either detect output or send notifications. TestProduct won’t be able to keep you informed until you’ve changed to a functioning sensor layer.
